items.title: Military-made AI tool helped thwart World Cup bomb threat - Federal News Network
items.summary:
A military-made artificial intelligence tool helped law enforcement thwart a bomb threat at the FIFA World Cup in California this summer.

The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. Ryan Hetrick, who leads the Pentagon’s Generative AI Task Force, said Nov. 6 at an AI event in Washington. [...] Hetrick pointed to a recent visit to the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, where he built an AI tool that cut the time it takes to execute a particular cyber operations workflow from 100 hours to 15. That tool is now available to all cyber officers across the department, he said.

“We don’t do policy shops. We don’t do PowerPoints. We go to the edge and build with the warfighter,” he said. “You can’t be building agents from the Pentagon.” [...] Three days earlier, Hetrick and colleagues from the Defense Department, FBI and Coast Guard had gathered at the White House to design an automated agent to write spot reports — short, time-sensitive narratives on quickly evolving situations — for the World Cup Task Force.

In case of a security incident, law enforcement on the ground would call the White House, and the World Cup task force would write up a spot report and send it up the chain of command to coordinate a response, Hetrick said.

items.title: The U.S.–China AI Competition: Two Paths to Artificial General Intelligence | Center for Security and Emerging Technology
items.summary:
November 9, 2026

The United States leads the world in frontier AI models and computing, but China is pursuing broader paths toward artificial general intelligence, including robotics, “embodiment,” and brain-inspired systems. A forthcoming CSET study compares the two countries’ strengths and asks what U.S. policymakers may miss when they treat AI competition as a single race.

## Executive Summary [...] Do not mistake today’s model rankings for a permanent strategic verdict. The paths to artificial general intelligence and superintelligence remain uncertain. China’s relative weakness in frontier compute coexists with strengths in engineering, deployment, and alternative research approaches. [...] The United States has a substantial lead in the computing resources and models driving today’s AI boom. Yet measuring the competition with China solely by the performance of large language models (LLMs) risks overlooking how China understands the goal and intends to reach it.

Our forthcoming CSET report argues that the two countries pursue different conceptions of artificial general intelligence (AGI).

items.title: SPS to tighten student tech policies this week for students in grades 3 to 5
items.summary:
SEATTLE — Seattle Public Schools (SPS) is tightening its technology rules for some students this week, adding new limits aimed at reducing distractions and curbing reliance on generative AI tools.

Superintendent Ben Shuldiner said that when he arrived in Seattle, it was clear the district had “steered too heavily into an overreliance of technology.” [...] Under the changes, students in grades three through five will have a one-hour daily cap on screen time. The limit includes activities such as watching a 10-minute educational video.

The district will also no longer allow iPads and laptops to be used as incentives or rewards. In addition, Seattle Public Schools is blocking access to Minecraft, YouTube and Gemini, programs Shuldiner said have been "abused." [...] RELATED | Seattle schools to cap elementary students' screen time, block unapproved AI tools

Parents have been asking the district to review how technology is used in classrooms, saying students are getting distracted or relying too heavily on generative AI tools.

Tôi là một trợ lý nghiên cứu đa năng được thiết kế để hỗ trợ bạn tìm kiếm thông tin, tài liệu và dữ liệu từ nhiều nguồn khác nhau.

- **Xử lý tài liệu và định dạng:** Tóm tắt, trích xuất văn bản từ URL, định dạng báo cáo và loại bỏ các liên kết trùng lặp.

The multi-agent orchestration framework can autonomously manage the full incident life cycle, starting from detection and intelligent triage to stakeholder communication, automated mitigation, and post-incident root cause analysis.

By leveraging agentic AI, Shah said, PayPal has reduced incident repair time from about 45 minutes to less than 5 minutes.

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
UC Berkeley, Vice Chancellor for Research Office

# Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics

November 9, 2026

By: Jason Pohl

Professor Ken Goldberg has long had doubts about how quickly robot capabilities could advance. But new AI models are leading to robotic innovations that give him "goosebumps."

 A large, blue robotic arm holds a small part over a series of buckets and containers. [...] In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] “AI-powered industrial robots must continuously improve reliability and performance,” said Jeff Mahler, Ambi Robotics’ co-founder and chief technology officer. “Agentic robotics converted production data into robot behavior updates, increasing throughput across our U.S. fleet while keeping engineers in control.”

items.title: Nvidia Reveals New Robot AI with 95% Success Rate in Tests - TipRanks.com
items.summary:
AI chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) introduced a new robotics AI model called GR00T 2 on Monday. The model achieved a 95% average success rate on 50 tasks after receiving just five demonstrations of each task. Even without specific demonstrations, the model managed to complete 40 of those 50 tasks at least once. In addition, Nvidia revealed its updated Isaac Lab 3.0 software at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, Texas. [...] According to Nvidia, GR00T 2 was trained on robot data and 100,000 hours of first-person point-of-view videos. This helps the model understand how humans interact with objects so that robots can learn similar skills.

For example, a person could demonstrate how to pick up an object or connect a cable. GR00T 2 could then learn that action and apply it to different types of robots without requiring each robot to demonstrate the task. [...] To help robots learn these skills, Nvidia also introduced improvements to Isaac Lab 3.0, which allows developers to train robots in computer simulations before testing them in the real world. The updated software can simulate how flexible objects behave, such as cables and clothing, which helps robots understand how objects move when they touch or grab them.

items.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
items.summary:
Investors have turned skeptical on the AI trade of late due to a combination of higher borrowing costs, concerns about soaring debt and public backlash towards the industry. The Nasdaq on Thursday suffered its steepest drop in 19 months, led by a plunge in shares of the chipmakers and neoclouds most closely tied to the AI buildout.

This is breaking news. Please refresh for updates. [...] OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar on Friday said the company will continue to invest in artificial intelligence infrastructure, even after voters strongly rebuked data centers during Tuesday's midterm elections. [...] OpenAI depends on data centers to train its AI models and serve customers, and Friar said she doesn't think the midterms dramatically changed anything for the company.

"If the midterm means more focus on data centers and communities, we're going to keep doing the work to get into those communities and to build trust with them," Friar said.
